title: Financial Services Charter
content: The Financial Services Interest Group brings together stakeholders from regulated financial institutions to identify where MCP needs to adapt for compliance, auditability, and risk-controlled deployment. It gathers use cases and requirements from the financial sector, develops and validates domain-specific extensions, and scopes problems with broad applicability into SEPs or Working Groups so that innovations proven in regulated environments can benefit the wider MCP ecosystem.

title: Financial Services Charter
content: Compliance and auditability: requirements for tamper-evident, portable records of what a tool call did, under what authority, and against which policy, so that MCP interactions can satisfy regulatory audit and incident-review obligations Data lineage and provenance: source attribution, citation, and consent metadata for data surfaced through MCP, so that downstream consumers can establish where information came from and on what basis it may be used Guardrails and attestation: verification frameworks and cryptographic attestations that let a regulated institution gain assurance about server identity, tool behavior, and the integrity of responses before acting on them Policy enforcement: declarative policies for tool usage and data handling, and the points at which they are enforced, so that institutions can encode regulatory and internal-control constraints as machine-checkable rules Finance-specific extensions: developing, maintaining, and gathering implementation experience on MCP extensions that address the above in the FSIG repository, including reference implementations and conformance testing Interoperability across institutions: common patterns and standards that allow regulated institutions to interoperate without each reinventing compliance plumbing SEP promotion: identifying extensions with applicability beyond financial services and shepherding them toward the core specification with core-maintainer sponsorship Regulatory liaison: translating constraints from regulators and industry bodies into concrete technical requirements and input for other groups

title: Scientific Computing Charter
content: The Scientific Computing Interest Group explores use cases for MCP in scientific and engineering workflows. The interest group gathers use cases from research and industry practitioners to understand any gaps that would warrant extension development or protocol improvements, which may lead to the formation of working groups.

title: Scientific Computing Charter
content: Quantities, units, uncertainty: representing physical quantities with units of measure, dimensional information, uncertainty in tool inputs and outputs, and quantity kinds, so that agents and clients can establish guardrails to enforce physical constraints Reproducibility and provenance: capturing the parameters, software and solver versions, and other inputs needed to reproduce computational results obtained through MCP Arrays and numerical datasets: conveying arrays, tensors, tabular data, and datasets that are too large for a model’s context, including how such payloads are referenced and passed to tools Long-running computation: simulations, solver runs, and batch or HPC job submission, and how they map onto MCP’s tasks architecture for asynchronous execution, progress, and cancellation mechanisms Interoperability with existing scientific standards: how MCP should relate to established domain formats, vocabularies, and ontologies rather than re-inventing them Cross-domain use-case determination: collecting requirements from physics, chemistry, biology, earth and climate science, astronomy, and engineering, and identifying recurring requirements

title: Scientific Computing Charter
content: Defining scientific data formats or vocabularies: unit systems, file formats, and domain ontologies are maintained by existing standards bodies and communities; this group discusses how MCP interoperates with them, not how they should be designed Building or maintaining domain MCP servers: individual servers for a particular software package, code, or dataset are valuable inputs to the group’s use-case gathering, but building them is not protocol work Authorization and identity mechanics: OAuth flows, scopes, and token handling belong to the Authorization IG

title: Scientific Computing Charter
content: Tasks and Events WG: Tasks are the foundation for the long-running simulation and job-submission workflows for high-performance computing Interceptors WG: interceptors are a potential implementation path for validating correctness and normalizing units between clients and servers File Uploads WG: input datasets, mesh and geometry files, and other large files must be considered Progressive Disclosure WG: scientific servers often expose large, hierarchical tool surfaces that motivate organization beyond flat lists Registry WG: publishing and discovering servers for shared scientific software and datasets intersects with registry metadata

title: Security Charter
content: The Security Interest Group is the first stop for MCP-specific security topics. It vets incoming threats, security-relevant proposals, and disclosure questions, then routes validated work to the Working Group or SEP that owns it.

title: Security Charter
content: Triage and routing: receiving security topics raised on Discord or GitHub and handing them to the owning group (Auth IG, Transports WG, Registry WG, Tool Annotations IG, SDK maintainers) Threat modeling: developing and maintaining a shared, layered view of MCP attack surfaces spanning admission and identity, caller governance, runtime behavior, interception and enforcement, and auditability, to give individual proposals a common frame of reference Server identity, attestation, and admission: requirements for establishing that a server is what it claims to be before a client dispatches to it, including signed assertions, trust roots, and the boundary between protocol-level and registry-level verification Supply chain and provenance: integrity of locally executed server binaries and packages (typosquatting, unpinned dependencies, unsigned artifacts) and how clients can verify what they spawn Runtime drift and post-admission change: treatment of tool, schema, or behavior changes after a server has been approved, and whether such changes are versioning, re-approval, or security events Auditability and observability: requirements for tamper-evident records of what a tool call did and under what authority, for compliance and incident review Transport-adjacent security: secrets handling, process isolation, and unauthenticated surface area for stdio and other non-HTTP transports where the HTTP authorization specification does not apply Security Best Practices documentation: authoring and reviewing entries in the Security Best Practices guidance, including liaising with external bodies such as OWASP GenAI and CoSAI on MCP-specific content Vulnerability disclosure routing: providing a known point of contact for reporters who have filed a private security advisory against an MCP repository and need help reaching the right maintainer

This group provides security requirements as input Registry service operation: running and securing the hosted Registry service belongs to the Registry WG. This group provides threat input on provenance and publishing Product-specific hardening guides: step-by-step configuration for individual host applications or cloud platforms is documentation for those products rather than protocol work Competitively sensitive or non-public business information, per the MCP Antitrust Policy

title: Project Policies
content: The standing policies that apply to everyone who takes part in the MCP project, and where each one is defined. This page lists the policies that apply to everyone who takes part in the MCP project: in meetings, on Discord, and in every repository under the modelcontextprotocol organization. Group Leads and Facilitators link it from meeting agendas.

title: Project Policies
content: The Code of Conduct governs every channel, repository and meeting. Send reports to mcp-coc@anthropic.com. The Community Moderators handle them under the Contributor Ladder and escalate to Core Maintainers when needed.

title: Project Policies
content: Participants often work for competing organizations. MCP is organized as Model Context Protocol a Series of LF Projects, LLC, so the LF Projects policies, including its antitrust policy, apply to all participants. The project’s own Antitrust Policy sets out how meetings and standard-setting discussions are conducted.

title: Project Policies
content: Code and specification contributions are made under the Apache License 2.0 and other documentation under CC-BY-4.0, with no copyright assignment. The governing text is General Project Policies.

title: Project Policies
content: Any AI assistance used for a contribution must be disclosed in the pull request or issue, together with its extent. This includes AI-written review responses and comments; trivial spacing or typo fixes are the only exception. The full policy is AI_POLICY.md, which applies to every repository in the organization.

title: Project Policies
content: Do not report security issues in public issues, discussions or pull requests. Open a private advisory on the affected repository at github.com/modelcontextprotocol/<repo>/security/advisories/new. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the specification repository and on every official SDK and project repository. Before filing, read SECURITY.md: it says what to include, describes the trust model and the behaviors that are intentional rather than vulnerabilities (stdio command execution, denial of service by a stdio peer, server side effects, LLM-driven tool invocation), and lists what remains in scope. A private advisory is also the project’s emergency security reporting mechanism. Report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents through a private advisory on the affected repository. State at the start of the report that the vulnerability is being actively exploited or that an incident is under way. The maintainers who receive a report coordinate the fix and advisory across every affected SDK so that advisories are released together, and raise it with the specification maintainers when the root cause is in the specification (see SDK Vulnerability Disclosure). CVEs are assigned through GitHub’s CNA. Questions that are not themselves a report, including which repository to file against, go to the Security Interest Group in #security-ig.

title: Project Policies
content: The Model Context Protocol project publishes software, including the official SDKs, that is ultimately intended for commercial activities. The project is supported under the Linux Foundation CRA stewardship framework. See the Linux Foundation’s CRA guidance for open source projects for more on what the CRA asks of projects like this one. Maintainers who learn of an actively exploited vulnerability or a severe incident, such as a compromise of the release process, must notify a Core Maintainer or Lead Maintainer immediately in #security-disclosures on Discord, while they fix the problem and never instead of fixing it. That Core Maintainer or Lead Maintainer contacts the Linux Foundation CRA steward at steward@linuxfoundation.org and works with the steward from then on, so the project speaks to the steward with one voice. The CRA sets short deadlines for the steward’s reports, starting with an early warning within 24 hours and a fuller notification within 72 hours. The advisory, if there is one, records when the project first learned of the problem and when the steward was notified. A vulnerability with no evidence of exploitation is not a CRA escalation event. Other maintainers do not contact the steward directly, and reporters must use a private advisory.

title: Project Policies
content: Communication sets out which channel is for what, when a channel may be private, and where decisions are recorded.

title: Communication
content: The MCP project's communication channels, when a channel may be private, and where decisions are recorded. This page sets out the project’s communication channels, when a channel may be private, and where decisions are recorded. It was adopted by SEP-994, a Specification Enhancement Proposal (SEP), and is changed by a Process SEP. The Code of Conduct governs every channel. If you are new to the project, start at Contributing.

title: Communication
content: Channel Use it for Discord Real-time coordination among contributors, including working group, interest group and SDK discussion Meeting calendar Open group and maintainer meetings. For how meetings run, see Meetings and channels GitHub Discussions Ideas, feature requests with rationale, questions, roadmap discussion, announcements and releases, and meeting agendas and notes (Meeting Notes category) GitHub Issues Reproducible bugs, scoped documentation tasks, and CI and release tasks, filed through the issue forms. SEPs are pull requests to seps/, not issues Security advisories Vulnerabilities. Never post one in a public channel Each SDK and project repository has its own issue tracker and Discord channel. Most have Discussions turned off and use Issues instead; this repository and the registry are the main exceptions. Vulnerability reports follow the Security Policy.

title: Communication
content: The MCP Contributor Discord is for people working on the protocol and its projects, and is where discussion of the protocol and its design starts. It is not a support channel: report a reproducible bug as an issue on the repository it affects, and start from the documentation for questions about using MCP. Do not market products or services on the server, and mention vendors only as examples relevant to the specification. Channels are named #general for project-wide discussion, #<name>-wg and #<name>-ig for each working group and interest group, and #<lang>-sdk-dev for each SDK. Other projects have a channel such as #inspector-dev. Propose a new group in #wg-ig-group-creation. Responses are best-effort. Channels are public by default. Private channels are restricted to designated maintainers and Community Moderators and exist only for security incidents (CVEs and protocol vulnerabilities), people and Code of Conduct matters, and coordination that needs an immediate or focused response from a limited audience. Some maintainer decision channels are read-only. A private channel is a temporary incident room, not a place for routine development. Matters concerning an individual contributor may remain private.

title: Communication
content: Discord is not the record. A Discord discussion heading toward a technical or governance decision must move to a GitHub Discussion. Every technical or governance decision, including a Core Maintainer outcome on a SEP, is written up in a Discussion with the notes label, or on the SEP’s pull request. Specification changes are also recorded in the changelog, and process changes in these community pages. A record names who decided, the context, the options considered, the rationale, and the next steps. For meeting agendas and notes, see Meetings and channels.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: How individual MCP specification features move through Active, Deprecated, and Removed states, and the timeline implementers can plan against. This page defines how a feature of the MCP specification is deprecated and later removed, and the obligations that follow for SDKs. It was adopted by SEP-2596, a Specification Enhancement Proposal (SEP), and is changed by a Process SEP. Features currently Deprecated or scheduled for removal are listed in the Deprecated registry.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: This policy governs features of the MCP core specification: protocol messages, capabilities, transports, schema types, and normative behavioral requirements. The revision lifecycle of the specification document itself (Draft, Current, Final) is defined in the versioning guide.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: A specification feature is in exactly one of three states: State Meaning Implementer expectation Active The feature is part of the Current specification revision. Implement per the feature’s normative requirements. Deprecated The feature remains in the specification but is scheduled for removal. A migration path is documented (see below). New implementations should not adopt the feature. Existing implementations should migrate before the earliest removal date. Removed The feature has been deleted from draft and will be absent from the next Current revision. It remains documented in the Final revision it last appeared in. Implementations targeting that next Current revision must not depend on the feature. A Deprecated feature may be restored to Active by a SEP that supersedes the deprecation SEP and documents the changed circumstances. Restoration follows the same approval path as deprecation. If the feature is later deprecated again, the minimum deprecation window in Deprecating a Feature is measured afresh from the revision in which the new deprecation takes effect.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: Removal from the specification does not oblige an SDK to drop the feature from releases. That timeline is governed by the SDK’s own revision-support policy.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: A feature may be proposed for deprecation when: it has been superseded by another feature that covers the same use cases, it presents a security, privacy, or interoperability risk that cannot be mitigated in place, ecosystem telemetry or SDK maintainer consensus indicates negligible adoption relative to its maintenance cost, the Core Maintainers deem it appropriate for any other reason. Deprecation requires a SEP (see SEP Guidelines). The deprecation SEP must: Identify the feature by name and link to its definition in schema.ts (where applicable) and the specification prose. State the rationale against the criteria above. Document the migration path, or state explicitly that none is required. If the migration path names a replacement feature, that feature must be Active in the revision in which the deprecation takes effect; the replacement and the deprecation may land in the same revision. Specify the minimum deprecation window: the number of months, at least twelve, that the feature must remain Deprecated. The feature’s earliest removal is the first specification revision released as Current on or after the window elapses. When the deprecation SEP is accepted, its author makes the following changes to the draft specification in the SEP’s pull request, and the sponsor verifies them before setting final (see SEP Guidelines): Add a @deprecated JSDoc tag to the feature’s entry in schema.ts, referencing the deprecation SEP and the revision in which the deprecation takes effect. Add a deprecation notice with the same information to the feature’s specification prose. Record the deprecation in that revision’s changelog.mdx under a “Deprecated” heading. “Deprecated” and “Removed” are standing changelog headings alongside Major/Minor/Other. List the feature in the deprecated registry with its deprecation SEP, the revision in which it became Deprecated, its migration path, and its earliest removal. The feature becomes Deprecated when the revision carrying these edits is

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: is released as Current (see versioning guide), and the minimum deprecation window is counted from that release, not from the date the SEP reaches Final. SEP-2577 is a worked example of a deprecation SEP.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: docs/specification/draft/deprecated.mdx is the single list of every feature in a Deprecated or Removed state.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: Once the revision in which a feature becomes Deprecated is released as Current, Tier 1 SDKs: Must mark the corresponding API surface deprecated using the language’s native mechanism (for example @Deprecated in Java, [Obsolete] in .NET, @deprecated JSDoc in TypeScript, the Deprecated: doc convention in Go) in their next release, referencing the deprecation SEP and the earliest removal date where the mechanism permits. Should emit a runtime warning when a deprecated feature is exercised, using the language’s idiomatic mechanism (for example Python’s DeprecationWarning, Node.js’s process.emitWarning, or a configurable logger). A Tier 1 SDK that consistently fails to surface a Deprecated feature is subject to tier relegation.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: After the minimum deprecation window has elapsed, Core Maintainers may remove the feature when preparing a release. The removal is recorded in changelog.mdx under the “Removed” heading and in the registry. Any change to the original deprecation or removal, such as extending or shortening the timeline (Expedited removal) or restoring the feature to Active (Feature states), requires a SEP. A feature may remain Deprecated indefinitely.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: The twelve-month minimum window may be shortened when the feature presents an active security risk, meaning a vulnerability with a published security advisory or documented in-the-wild exploitation for which no in-place mitigation exists. Shortening the window requires Core Maintainer approval under the governance decision process, recorded in the deprecation SEP or, where the risk surfaces after that SEP is already Final, in a short expedited-removal SEP that references it. The shortened window must still provide at least ninety days between the feature becoming Deprecated and its earliest removal.

title: Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation
content: Any contributor may propose a deprecation, extension, or restoration through a SEP with a sponsor (see SEP Guidelines). Core Maintainers approve deprecations, removal timing, extensions, restorations, and expedited removals under the governance decision process, subject to Lead Maintainer veto (see Governance).

title: SDK Tiers
content: What each SDK tier requires, how conformance is measured, how an SDK moves between tiers, and the issue labels SDK repositories must use. This page defines the three SDK tiers, what each requires, how an SDK moves between them, and the issue labels SDK repositories must use. The tiers were adopted by SEP-1730, a Specification Enhancement Proposal (SEP), and are changed by a Process SEP. The SDK Working Group operates them, and each SDK’s current tier is shown on the SDKs page.

title: SDK Tiers
content: Tier 1 SDKs are fully supported and implement every non-experimental feature, including optional capabilities such as sampling and elicitation. SDKs in Tier 2 are actively maintained and working toward full specification support, and those in Tier 3 are experimental, partially implemented, or specialized. Experimental features and protocol extensions (such as Tasks and MCP Apps) are not required for any tier. Requirement Tier 1: Fully Supported Tier 2: Commitment to Full Support Tier 3: Experimental Conformance Tests 100% pass rate 80% pass rate No minimum New Protocol Features Before new spec version release, timeline agreed per release based on feature complexity Within 6 months No timeline commitment Issue Triage Within 2 business days Within a month No requirement Critical Bug Resolution Within 7 days Within two weeks No requirement Stable Release Required with clear versioning At least one stable release Not required Documentation Comprehensive with examples for all features Basic documentation covering core features No minimum Dependency Policy Published update policy Published update policy Not required Roadmap Published roadmap Published plan toward Tier 1 or explanation for remaining Tier 2 Not required Issue Triage means labeling an issue and determining whether it is valid, not resolving it. Critical Bug means a P0 issue as defined under Priority labels. Stable Release means a published version explicitly marked as production-ready, for example version 1.0.0 or higher without a pre-release identifier such as -alpha, -beta, or -rc. Clear Versioning means following idiomatic versioning patterns with a documented breaking-change policy. Roadmap means a published set of concrete steps and work items tracking implementation of the required specification components (non-experimental features and optional capabilities, as scoped under Conformance testing).

title: SDK Tiers
content: Conformance is measured with the conformance test suite. Each official SDK runs the suite against its default branch and publishes the results. The pass rates in the matrix are calculated against applicable required tests only: Tests for the specification version the SDK targets Excluding tests marked as pending or skipped Excluding tests for experimental features Excluding legacy backward-compatibility tests (unless the SDK claims legacy support) Excluding tests labeled disputed in the conformance repository, until the dispute is resolved Sustained test failures are handled under Tier relegation.

title: SDK Tiers
content: To request a higher tier, an SDK’s maintainers: Self-assess the SDK against the tier requirements. Open an issue in the modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol repository with the supporting evidence. Pass the conformance threshold for the requested tier on the latest stable release. Obtain approval from the SDK Working Group. The SDK Working Group makes the final tier assignment and records the decision and rationale as set out in its charter.

title: SDK Tiers
content: An SDK may be moved to a lower tier if existing conformance tests on its latest stable release fail continuously for 4 weeks: Tier 1 to Tier 2: any conformance test fails. Tier 2 to Tier 3: more than 20% of conformance tests fail. An SDK may also be relegated if issues remain unaddressed for two months. The SDK Working Group may likewise relegate a Tier 1 SDK that consistently fails to surface specification deprecations as required by Tier 1 SDK Obligations. The group decides each relegation and records it with its rationale.

title: SDK Tiers
content: SDK repositories must use the labels below. Two tier metrics are computed from them: triage response time (issue creation to first label) and critical bug resolution time (P0 label to close).

title: SDK Tiers
content: Label Description bug Something isn’t working enhancement Request for new feature question Further information requested Repositories using GitHub’s native issue types satisfy this requirement without type labels.

title: SDK Tiers
content: Use these exact label names in every repository. Label Description needs confirmation Unclear if still relevant needs repro Insufficient information to reproduce ready for work Has enough information to start good first issue Good for newcomers help wanted Contributions welcome from those familiar with codebase

title: SDK Tiers
content: Label Description P0 Critical: core functionality failures or high-severity security P1 Significant bug affecting many users P2 Moderate issues, valuable feature requests P3 Nice to haves, rare edge cases A P0 issue is either: A security vulnerability with a CVSS score of 7.0 or higher (High or Critical severity) A core functionality failure that prevents basic MCP operations: connection establishment, message exchange, or use of the core primitives (tools, resources, prompts)

title: Antitrust Policy
content: MCP Project Antitrust Policy for participants and contributors Effective: September 29, 2025 This policy applies to MCP meetings, working groups, interest groups, and any other project forum where competitors may be present. See Meetings and channels for how group meetings are run.

title: Antitrust Policy
content: The goal of the Model Context Protocol open source project (the “Project”) is to develop a universal standard for model-to-world interactions, including enabling LLMs and agents to seamlessly connect with and utilize external data sources and tools. The purpose of this Antitrust Policy (the “Policy”) is to avoid antitrust risks in carrying out this pro-competitive mission. Participants in and contributors to the Project (collectively, “participants”) will use their best reasonable efforts to comply in all respects with all applicable state and federal antitrust and trade regulation laws, and applicable antitrust/competition laws of other countries (collectively, the “Antitrust Laws”). The goal of Antitrust Laws is to encourage vigorous competition. Nothing in this Policy prohibits or limits the ability of participants to make, sell or use any product, or otherwise to compete in the marketplace. This Policy provides general guidance on compliance with Antitrust Law. Participants should contact their respective legal counsel to address specific questions. This Policy is conservative and is intended to promote compliance with the Antitrust Laws, not to create duties or obligations beyond what the Antitrust Laws actually require. In the event of any inconsistency between this Policy and the Antitrust Laws, the Antitrust Laws preempt and control.

title: Antitrust Policy
content: Technical participation in the Project shall be open to all, subject only to compliance with the provisions of the Project’s charter and other governance documents.

title: Antitrust Policy
content: At meetings among actual or potential competitors, there is a risk that participants in those meetings may improperly disclose or discuss information in violation of the Antitrust Laws or otherwise act in an anti-competitive manner. To avoid this risk, participants must adhere to the following policies when participating in Project-related or sponsored meetings, conference calls, or other forums (collectively, “Project Meetings”). Participants must not, in fact or appearance, discuss or exchange information regarding: An individual company’s current or projected prices, price changes, price differentials, markups, discounts, allowances, terms and conditions of sale, including credit terms, etc., or data that bear on prices, including profits, margins or cost. Industry-wide pricing policies, price levels, price changes, differentials, or the like. Actual or projected changes in industry production, capacity or inventories. Matters relating to bids or intentions to bid for particular products, procedures for responding to bid invitations or specific contractual arrangements. Plans of individual companies concerning the design, characteristics, production, distribution, marketing or introduction dates of particular products, including proposed territories or customers. Matters relating to actual or potential individual suppliers that might have the effect of excluding them from any market or of influencing the business conduct of firms toward such suppliers. Matters relating to actual or potential customers that might have the effect of influencing the business conduct of firms toward such customers. Individual company current or projected cost of procurement, development or manufacture of any product. Individual company market shares for any product or for all products. Confidential or otherwise sensitive business plans or strategy. In connection with all Project Meetings, participants must do the following: Adhere to prepared agendas. Insist that meeting minutes be

title: Antitrust Policy
content: be prepared and distributed to all participants, and that meeting minutes accurately reflect the matters that transpired. Consult with their respective counsel on all antitrust questions related to Project Meetings. Protest against any discussions that appear to violate these policies or the Antitrust Laws, leave any meeting in which such discussions continue, and either insist that such protest be noted in the minutes.

title: Antitrust Policy
content: The Project may establish standards, technical requirements and/or specifications for use (collectively, “requirements”). Participants shall not enter into agreements that prohibit or restrict any participant from establishing or adopting any other requirements. Participants shall not undertake any efforts, directly or indirectly, to prevent any firm from manufacturing, selling, or supplying any product not conforming to a requirement. The Project shall not promote standardization of commercial terms, such as terms for license and sale.

title: Antitrust Policy
content: To contact the Project regarding matters addressed by this Antitrust Policy, please send an email to antitrust@modelcontextprotocol.io, and reference “Antitrust Policy” in the subject line.

title: 架构概览
content: 本页是社区维护的非官方中文译文，不代表 MCP 官方。原文：Model Context Protocol 项目的英文页面（上游提交 ac00313f），© Model Context Protocol a Series of LF Projects, LLC.，按 CC-BY-4.0 授权。本页由原文翻译成中文，并按同一许可发布。如有出入，以英文原文为准。 本文概述 Model Context Protocol（MCP）的范围和核心概念，并通过一个示例逐一演示这些核心概念。 MCP SDK 已经替你处理了许多细节，因此对大多数开发者来说，最有用的可能是数据层协议一节。它介绍了 MCP 服务器如何向 AI 应用提供上下文。 具体的实现细节，请参阅你所用语言的 SDK 文档。

title: 架构概览
content: Model Context Protocol 包括以下几个项目： MCP 规范：MCP 的规范文档，规定了客户端和服务器的实现要求。 MCP SDK：用不同编程语言实现 MCP 的 SDK。 MCP 开发工具：用于开发 MCP 服务器和客户端的工具，包括 MCP Inspector MCP 参考服务器实现：MCP 服务器的参考实现。 MCP 只关注上下文交换的协议本身，并不规定 AI 应用如何使用 LLM，也不规定如何管理所提供的上下文。

title: 架构概览
content: MCP 采用客户端-服务器架构：MCP 宿主（Host），即 Claude Code 或 Claude Desktop 这样的 AI 应用，与一个或多个 MCP 服务器建立连接。具体做法是，MCP 宿主为每个 MCP 服务器各创建一个 MCP 客户端，每个 MCP 客户端与对应的 MCP 服务器保持一条专用连接。 使用 STDIO 传输的本地 MCP 服务器通常只服务一个 MCP 客户端；而使用 Streamable HTTP 传输的远程 MCP 服务器通常会同时服务许多 MCP 客户端。 MCP 架构中的主要参与者有： MCP 宿主：协调和管理一个或多个 MCP 客户端的 AI 应用 MCP 客户端：一个组件，负责与某个 MCP 服务器保持连接，并从该服务器获取上下文供 MCP 宿主使用 MCP 服务器：向 MCP 客户端提供上下文的程序 举个例子：Visual Studio Code 就是一个 MCP 宿主。当 Visual Studio Code 连接到某个 MCP 服务器（例如 Sentry MCP 服务器）时，Visual Studio Code 运行时会实例化一个 MCP 客户端对象，由它维持与 Sentry MCP 服务器的连接。 之后 Visual Studio Code 再连接另一个 MCP 服务器（例如本地文件系统服务器）时，Visual Studio Code 运行时会再实例化一个 MCP 客户端对象来维持这条连接。 注意，MCP 服务器指的是提供上下文数据的程序，与它运行在哪里无关。MCP 服务器既可以在本地运行，也可以在远程运行。例如，Claude Desktop 启动文件系统服务器时，这个服务器使用 STDIO 传输，因此运行在同一台机器上，这通常称为”本地” MCP 服务器。官方的 Sentry MCP 服务器运行在 Sentry 平台上，使用 Streamable HTTP 传输，这通常称为”远程” MCP 服务器。

title: 架构概览
content: MCP 由两层组成： 数据层：定义基于 JSON-RPC 的客户端-服务器通信协议，包括能力与版本的发现，以及工具、资源、提示词模板和通知等核心原语。 传输层：定义客户端与服务器之间交换数据所用的通信机制和通道，包括各传输方式特有的连接建立、消息分帧和授权。 从概念上说，数据层是内层，传输层是外层。 数据层 数据层实现了一套基于 JSON-RPC 2.0 的交换协议，定义了消息的结构和语义。 这一层包括： 发现：客户端可以通过 server/discover 请求，查询服务器支持的协议版本、能力和身份信息 服务器功能：让服务器提供核心功能，包括供 AI 执行操作的工具、提供上下文数据的资源，以及用于客户端交互的提示词模板 客户端功能：让服务器能够向用户征询输入。 辅助功能：支持其他附加能力，例如实时更新通知、长时间运行操作的进度跟踪 传输层 传输层负责客户端与服务器之间的通信通道和身份认证，处理 MCP 参与者之间的连接建立、消息分帧和安全通信。 MCP 支持两种传输机制： Stdio 传输：通过标准输入/输出流，在同一台机器上的本地进程之间直接通信。没有网络开销，性能最好。 Streamable HTTP 传输：客户端发往服务器的消息使用 HTTP POST，并可选用 Server-Sent Events 实现流式传输。这种传输方式支持与远程服务器通信，也支持标准的 HTTP 认证方式，包括 bearer 令牌、API 密钥和自定义请求头。MCP 推荐使用 OAuth 获取认证令牌。 传输层把通信细节与协议层隔离开来，使所有传输机制都能使用同一种 JSON-RPC 2.0 消息格式。

title: 架构概览
content: MCP 的核心之一，是定义 MCP 客户端与 MCP 服务器之间的数据模式和语义。开发者最感兴趣的可能就是数据层，尤其是其中的原语。正是这一部分规定了开发者可以通过哪些方式，把上下文从 MCP 服务器共享给 MCP 客户端。 MCP 以 JSON-RPC 2.0 作为底层的 RPC 协议。客户端发送请求，服务器作出响应。服务器可以通过多轮往返请求模式向客户端索取输入。不需要响应时，可以使用通知。 无状态与发现 MCP 是一种。每个请求都在 _meta 字段中携带协议版本，以及与该请求相关的，因此服务器可以独立处理每一个请求。除非另有配置，客户端还应在同一字段中标明自己的身份。服务器通过必须实现的 server/discover 请求声明自己支持的版本和能力，客户端可以在发送其他请求之前先发这个请求。详细信息见规范，示例中也演示了每个请求附带的元数据和发现流程。 原语 原语是 MCP 中最重要的概念，它定义了客户端和服务器可以相互提供什么：可以与 AI 应用共享哪些类型的上下文信息，以及可以执行哪些操作。 MCP 定义了三种可由服务器暴露的核心原语： 工具：AI 应用可以调用来执行操作的可执行函数（例如文件操作、API 调用、数据库查询） 资源：为 AI 应用提供上下文信息的数据源（例如文件内容、数据库记录、API 响应） 提示词模板：帮助组织与语言模型交互的可复用模板（例如系统提示词、少样本示例） 每种原语都有对应的方法：用于发现的（*/list），以及用于获取（resources/read、prompts/get）或执行（tools/call）的。 MCP 客户端用 */list 方法发现可用的原语。例如，客户端可以先列出可用的工具（tools/list），把它们提供给模型，再执行模型调用的那些工具（tools/call）。这样的设计让列表可以是动态的。 举一个具体的例子：假设有一个提供数据库相关上下文的 MCP 服务器。它可以暴露用于查询数据库的工具、一个包含数据库模式（schema）的资源，以及一个包含少样本示例、指导如何使用这些工具的提示词模板。 关于服务器原语的更多细节，请参阅服务器概念。 MCP 还定义了可由客户端暴露的原语，让 MCP 服务器的作者能够构建更丰富的交互。 征询（Elicitation）：允许服务器向用户请求更多信息。当服务器作者需要从用户那里获取更多信息，或需要用户确认某个操作时，这一原语很有用。服务器通过 elicitation/create 方法请求用户输入。 征询请求通过多轮往返请求模式传递，详见征询概述。 关于客户端原语的更多细节，请参阅客户端概念。 自协议版本 2026-07-28 起，客户端功能中的根目录（roots）和采样（sampling），以及服务器功能中的协议日志，均已弃用。新的实现应改用以下替代方案： 根目录：通过工具参数、资源 URI 或服务器配置传入目录或文件。 采样：直接对接 LLM 提供商的 API。协议没有为”通过客户端请求模型生成”定义替代机制。 日志：stdio 服务器输出到 stderr，或使用 OpenTelemetry。 除了服务器原语和客户端原语，协议还支持构建在核心协议之上的可选扩展。例如，任务（Tasks）扩展允许服务器为长时间运行的请求返回一个持久的句柄，客户端可以据此轮询状态，并在之后获取结果。 通知 协议支持实时通知，让服务器和客户端之间可以动态更新。例如，当服务器的可用工具发生变化（比如有新功能可用，或现有工具被修改）时，服务器可以发送工具更新通知，告知已连接的客户端。通知以 JSON-RPC 2.0 通知消息的形式发送（不期待响应）。变更通知需要主动订阅：客户端打开一个长期存在的 subscriptions/listen 流，列出想接收的通知类型，服务器就在这个流上推送匹配的通知。

title: 架构概览
content: 本节以数据层协议为重点，一步步演示 MCP 客户端与服务器的交互过程。我们会用 JSON-RPC 2.0 消息演示发现、工具操作和通知。 1 发现 如无状态与发现一节所述，每个 MCP 请求都在 _meta 字段中携带协议版本和客户端能力，客户端还应在其中附上自己的身份。如果客户端想在发出其他请求之前先了解服务器支持什么，就发送 server/discover 请求，每个服务器都必须实现这个请求。发现结果通常可以缓存，也就是说可以重复使用，不必每次请求前都走一遍发现流程。 { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "server/discover", "params": { "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28", "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": { "name": "example-client", "version": "1.0.0" }, "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": { "elicitation": {} } } } } { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": { "resultType": "complete", "supportedVersions": ["2026-07-28"], "capabilities": { "tools": { "listChanged": true }, "resources": {} }, "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo": { "name": "example-server", "version": "1.0.0" } }, "ttlMs": 3600000, "cacheScope": "public" } } 理解发现交换 _meta 字段和发现响应共同起到以下几个作用： 协议版本选择：io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion 字段声明客户端在这次请求中使用的版本，响应中的 supportedVersions 列出服务器接受的版本。如果服务器不支持所请求的版本，它会以 UnsupportedProtocolVersionError 拒绝请求，并列出自己支持的版本，客户端再用双方都支持的版本重试。 能力发现：客户端在每个请求的 io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities 中声明自己的能力，服务器则在 server/discover 的结果中返回自己的 capabilities 对象。这样双方都知道对方能处理哪些原语（工具、资源、提示词模板），以及是否提供变更通知，从而不会尝试对方不支持的操作。 身份交换：请求 _meta 中的 io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo 字段和结果 _meta 中的 io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo 字段提供身份和版本信息，用于调试和兼容性处理。 这个例子中的交换展示了 MCP 能力是如何声明的：客户端能力： "elicitation": {}：客户端声明，当服务器请求时，它可以向用户收集额外的输入 服务器能力： "tools": {"listChanged": true}：服务器支持工具原语，并且能够响应 subscriptions/listen 中的 toolsListChanged 过滤条件。请求了这个过滤条件的客户端，会在工具列表变化时收到 notifications/tools/list_changed。 "resources": {}：服务器还支持资源原语（可以处理 resources/list 和 resources/read 方法） 调用 server/discover 是可选的。因为每个请求都携带同样的 _meta 字段，客户端完全可以直接发送任何请求，如果收到版本错误再处理即可。发现只是一种便捷方式，用一个请求就能拿到服务器的身份、能力和支持的版本。 在 AI 应用中如何运作 AI 应用的 MCP 客户端管理器连接到已配置的服务器，并保存发现到的能力以备后用。应用据此判断哪些服务器能提供哪类功能（工具、资源、提示词模板），以及它们是否支持实时更新。在 Python SDK 中，发现在客户端建立连接时就会完成，结果随后可以从客户端对象上读取。 Pseudo-code for AI application discovery # 工具发现（原语） 客户端可以发送 tools/list 请求来发现可用的工具。这个请求是 MCP 工具发现机制的基础：客户端借此在尝试使用工具之前，先了解服务器上有哪些工具可用。 { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "method": "tools/list", "params": { "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28", "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": { "name": "example-client", "version": "1.0.0" }, "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": { "elicitation": {} } } } } { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": { "resultType": "complete", "tools": [ { "name": "calculator_arithmetic", "title": "Calculator", "description": "Perform mathematical calculations including basic arithmetic, trigonometric functions, and algebraic operations", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "expression": { "type": "string", "description": "Mathematical expression to evaluate (e.g., '2 + 3 * 4', 'sin(30)', 'sqrt(16)')" } }, "required": ["expression"] } }, { "name": "weather_current", "title": "Weather Information", "description": "Get current weather information for any location worldwide", "inputSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "location": { "type": "string", "description": "City name, address, or coordinates (latitude,longitude)" }, "units": { "type": "string", "enum": ["metric", "imperial", "kelvin"], "description": "Temperature units to use in response", "default": "metric" } }, "required": ["location"] } } ], "ttlMs": 300000, "cacheScope": "public", "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo": { "name": "example-server", "version": "1.0.0" } } } } 理解工具发现请求 除了每个 MCP 请求都附带的标准 _meta 字段外，tools/list 请求不需要其他参数。它还接受一个可选的 cursor 参数用于分页，上面的示例省略了这个参数。 理解工具发现响应 响应中包含一个 tools 数组，为每个可用工具提供完整的元数据。这种基于数组的结构让服务器可以同时暴露多个工具，并且不同功能之间的边界清晰。响应中的每个工具对象都包含几个关键字段： name：工具在该服务器命名空间内的唯一标识符。它是执行工具时使用的主键，应遵循清晰的命名方式（例如用 calculator_arithmetic，而不是简单的 calculate） title：便于人阅读的工具显示名称，客户端可以展示给用户

content: title：便于人阅读的工具显示名称，客户端可以展示给用户 description：详细说明工具做什么、什么时候该用 inputSchema：定义预期输入参数的 JSON Schema，既可以用于类型校验，也清楚地说明了哪些参数必填、哪些可选 结果标记为 "resultType": "complete"，并带有两个缓存字段。ttlMs 是以毫秒为单位的新鲜度提示，表示这份工具列表可以缓存五分钟；cacheScope 表示谁可以复用这个响应。完整规则见规范中的缓存。 在 AI 应用中如何运作 AI 应用从所有已连接的 MCP 服务器获取可用工具，合并成一个统一的工具注册表，供语言模型访问。这样 LLM 就能知道自己可以执行哪些操作，并在对话中自动生成相应的工具调用。 Pseudo-code for AI application tool discovery # Pseudo-code using MCP Python SDK patterns available_tools = [] for client in app.mcp_clients(): tools_response = await client.list_tools() available_tools.extend(tools_response.tools) conversation.register_available_tools(available_tools) 同时接入很多服务器的客户端，可以采用渐进式工具发现，而不是一开始就加载全部工具。 3 工具执行（原语） 现在客户端可以用 tools/call 方法执行工具了。这一步演示了 MCP 原语在实践中的用法：发现可用工具之后，客户端就可以带上合适的参数调用它们。 理解工具执行请求 tools/call 请求采用结构化的格式，确保类型安全，也让客户端和服务器之间的通信清晰明确。注意，这里用的是发现响应中给出的正式工具名（weather_current），而不是简化的名字： { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "weather_current", "arguments": { "location": "San Francisco", "units": "imperial" }, "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28", "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": { "name": "example-client", "version": "1.0.0" }, "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": { "elicitation": {} } } } } { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 3, "result": { "resultType": "complete", "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Current weather in San Francisco: 68°F, partly cloudy with light winds from the west at 8 mph. Humidity: 65%" } ], "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo": { "name": "example-server", "version": "1.0.0" } } } } 工具执行的关键要素 请求结构包括以下几个重要部分： name：必须与发现响应中的工具名（weather_current）完全一致，这样服务器才能准确识别要执行哪个工具。 arguments：包含工具 inputSchema 中定义的输入参数。在这个例子中： location：“San Francisco”（必填参数） units：“imperial”（可选参数，未指定时默认为 “metric”） _meta：携带每个请求的标准字段，即每个 MCP 请求都必须包含的协议版本和客户端能力，以及客户端的身份（除非另有配置，客户端应当附上）。 JSON-RPC 结构：使用标准的 JSON-RPC 2.0 格式，用唯一的 id 关联请求和响应。 理解工具执行响应 响应展示了 MCP 灵活的内容体系： content 数组：工具响应返回一个内容对象数组，可以包含丰富的多种格式（文本、图片、资源等） 内容类型：每个内容对象都有一个 type

title: 架构概览
content: type 字段。在这个例子中，"type": "text" 表示文本内容。工具结果还可以包含图片（image）、音频（audio）、资源链接（resource_link）和嵌入资源（resource）。并不是每个模型都支持所有这些类型，因此客户端可能需要处理模型不支持的内容。 结构化内容（可选）：工具还可以返回结构化内容，即结果中 structuredContent 字段里的一个 JSON 值。本例中的工具只返回了文本。 这种执行模式让 AI 应用可以动态调用服务器的功能，并把收到的响应融入与语言模型的对话中。 在 AI 应用中如何运作 当语言模型在对话中决定使用某个工具时，AI 应用会拦截这次工具调用，把它路由到相应的 MCP 服务器并执行，再把结果作为对话的一部分返回给 LLM。这样 LLM 就能获取实时数据，并在外部世界中执行操作。 # Pseudo-code for AI application tool execution async def handle_tool_call(conversation, tool_name, arguments): client = app.find_mcp_client_for_tool(tool_name) result = await client.call_tool(tool_name, arguments) conversation.add_tool_result(result.content) 4 实时更新（通知） MCP 支持实时通知，服务器无需等待客户端轮询，就能主动告知变化。这一步演示通知系统，它是让客户端保持同步、及时响应的关键功能。 订阅变更 变更通知需要主动订阅。要接收通知，客户端发送一个 subscriptions/listen 请求，打开一个长期存在的通知流，并在 notifications 过滤条件中列出想接收的事件类型。这里客户端请求的是工具列表变更： Listen Request { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 4, "method": "subscriptions/listen", "params": { "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28", "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": { "name": "example-client", "version": "1.0.0" }, "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": { "elicitation": {} } }, "notifications": { "toolsListChanged": true } } } 每个客户端请求都在 _meta 中携带 io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion 和 io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities 字段，通常还带有 io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo，因此服务器无需依赖连接状态就能识别客户端。服务器用 notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged 确认订阅。这是第一条在 _meta 中携带该订阅 ID 的消息（在它之前，服务器不会为这个订阅发送任何其他通知）。其中的 notifications 字段反映服务器同意响应的那部分过滤条件，不支持的通知类型会被省略： Acknowledgment { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged", "params": { "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId": 4 }, "notifications": { "toolsListChanged": true } } } 理解工具列表变更通知 确认之后，每当服务器的可用工具发生变化（例如有新功能可用、现有工具被修改，或某些工具暂时不可用），服务器就会在这个流上推送一条通知： Notification { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/tools/list_changed", "params": { "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId": 4 } } } MCP 通知的关键特性 无需响应：注意通知中没有 id 字段。这遵循

title: 架构概览
content: 字段。这遵循 JSON-RPC 2.0 的通知语义，既不期待也不会发送响应。 主动订阅：只有在 subscriptions/listen 过滤条件中请求了 "toolsListChanged": true 的客户端才会收到这条通知，而且只有在工具能力中声明了 "listChanged": true 的服务器才提供它（见第 1 步）。 订阅 ID 标记：流上的每条通知都在 _meta 中携带 io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId，值为打开这个流的 subscriptions/listen 请求的 JSON-RPC ID（本例中为 4），这样客户端就能把每条通知与产生它的订阅对应起来。 事件驱动：服务器根据内部状态的变化决定何时发送通知，让 MCP 连接保持动态、响应及时。 尽力而为：不保证每条通知都会被发送或收到，尤其是在传输重连的时候。客户端还应配合轮询，确保结果是最新的。 客户端如何响应通知 收到这条通知后，客户端通常会重新请求工具列表。这形成了一个刷新循环，让客户端对可用工具的了解始终保持最新： Request { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 5, "method": "tools/list", "params": { "_meta": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28", "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo": { "name": "example-client", "version": "1.0.0" }, "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": { "elicitation": {} } } } } 为什么通知很重要 这套通知系统之所以重要，有以下几个原因： 动态环境：工具可能随服务器状态、外部依赖或用户权限的变化而增减 效率：有更新时客户端会收到通知，因此可以减少轮询 一致性：帮助客户端及时更新对服务器可用能力的认识 实时协作：让 AI 应用能够及时响应、适应不断变化的上下文 这种通知模式不只适用于工具，也适用于其他 MCP 原语，从而实现客户端与服务器之间全面的实时同步。 在 AI 应用中如何运作 AI 应用为自己关心的变更保持一个打开的通知流。收到通知后，它会立即刷新工具注册表，并更新 LLM 可用的能力。这样进行中的对话总能用上最新的工具集，LLM 也能在新功能可用时动态适应。 # Pseudo-code for AI application notification handling async def follow_tool_changes(client): async with client.listen(tools_list_changed=True) as sub: async for _event in sub: tools_response = await client.list_tools() app.update_available_tools(client, tools_response.tools) if app.conversation.is_active(): app.conversation.notify_llm_of_new_capabilities()
